title: Incremental compatibility classification and rollback policy for serving runtime
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Proposal and implementation plan for a formalized incremental compatibility classifier, clear rules for what counts as a breaking vs non-breaking change, LTS channel behavior, and an automated rollback/runbook integration for serving runtime releases. This ticket produces the policy text plus an initial compatibility-checker CLI and CI gating job that enforces the policy on merging changes to runtime main and release branches. Primary goals: 1) reduce accidental breaking changes entering hosted or dedicated deployments, 2) shorten detection-to-rollback time when regressions occur, 3) provide teams with a clear migration window and tooling to automate client updates.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Documented compatibility classification matrix describing 5 change classes and exact contract expectations for each class. 2) CI job 'compat-check' that runs model of API diff + binary interface checks and fails on 'breaking' class unless release-override label present. 3) Canary rollout gates implemented in CD pipeline: health, latency p95, token throughput, correctness smoke tests. 4) Rollback playbook wired into on-call runbooks with automated circuit-breaker that can revert to previous runtime version within 5 minutes and notify stakeholders. 5) Compatibility-checker CLI published in github.com/redwood-inference/compat-check v0.1 with README and example usages. 6) Migration notes and deprecation headers generated automatically for clients when a deprecation is introduced.
policy_summary: We adopt a contract-first, classifier-driven semver policy for the serving runtime. Changes are categorized as: SAFE (non-functional changes, config defaults), MINOR-EXTENSION (additive APIs, optional fields), BEHAVIORAL (non-backwards-compatible behavior change without schema change), CONFIG-IMPACT (default switch that may change behavior), BREAKING (protocol/ABI/API incompatibility). Only BREAKING changes increment major, MINOR-EXTENSION and BEHAVIORAL increment minor, SAFE increments patch. Deprecations are announced with a minimum 90-day window for hosted and 180-day window for Dedicated/Private customers unless opt-in accelerated migration is negotiated.
rollout_gates_and_metrics: Canary -> Gradual -> Full. Gates enforced by CD: (A) Service health (no new 5xx for 15m, error rate delta < 2x baseline), (B) Latency SLOs (p95 within 1.25x baseline), (C) Token throughput sanity (within expected throughput range), (D) Regression checks using canary prompt suite (false positive rate < 0.5%). Gate thresholds are configurable per release via release metadata. Dashboard: runtime/releases/ENG-12847 on Grafana. Automated abort if any gate fails; automatic rollback if abort persists beyond 10 minutes.
compatibility_classifier_examples: Examples: 1) Add a new optional JSON field to request proto -> MINOR-EXTENSION. 2) Remove a previously-documented header -> BREAKING. 3) Change default batch size from 16 to 32 -> CONFIG-IMPACT (requires migration note). 4) Rename an internal enum value that is not surfaced to clients -> SAFE. 5) Change tokenization behavior in a model-serving binary -> BEHAVIORAL (non-obvious regressions; treated like MINOR-EXTENSION unless it alters API tokens returned).
migration_and_deprecation_rules: - All deprecated endpoints/fields must emit 'Deprecation' response header with version and removal date. - Deprecation windows: hosted 90d, dedicated/private 180d. - During window, SDKs print warnings for consumers and provide migration helpers. - For LTS branches, deprecations are only allowed for removal after LTS-2 backport window and require explicit RFC approval.
upgrade_tooling_plan: Deliverables: 1) compat-check CLI that runs API diffs, proto/schema checks, ABI checks for runtime shared libs, and a heuristic behavior-sim test using the canonical prompt set. 2) CI integration in Github Actions to block merges. 3) amcli extension with `amcli runtime upgrade-preview` to show customers a migration diff and estimated impact. 4) Release notes templates and automated deprecation header generation. 5) Canary job templates for infra teams.
ci_and_premerge_enforcement: - New job `compat-check` in runtime repo must pass before merge to main/release. - Maintainers can add 'compat-override' label for explicit major bumps but must attach an RFC link and an approved migration plan. - Unit tests required: compatibility regression unit tests and end-to-end smoke against a local emulator. - Backwards-compatibility suite to run nightly across last 3 released runtime versions.
rollback_runbook_summary: 1) Detection: CD gate fails OR observability alert triggers. 2) Immediate step: pause rollout, notify on-call, open incident. 3) If failure persists > 10 min, execute automated rollback job to previous tag (uses immutable image tags). 4) Post-rollback: capture traces, logs, and the failing canary request set; run offline diff to root-cause. 5) Follow-up: patch branch with revert or corrective changes and schedule hotfix release. 6) Communication: status page update and customer email if impact > medium.
operational_considerations: - Dedicated/Private customers: provide a 'pre-approve' channel for breaking changes; if pre-approval not granted, change must be gated on dedicated release window. - LTS channel: only patch and critical fixes are backported; new features classified MINOR-EXTENSION are allowed as opt-in. - Backward-compatibility matrix maintained in DOCS: runtime/compatibility-matrix.md and kept in sync by CI. - Telemetry: compute compatibility_score per PR and store in release metadata.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: false negatives in classifier (missed breaking change) -> mitigation: run nightly compatibility sweep across production traces. Risk: slower throughput for premerge due to heavy checks -> mitigation: sampling + fast heuristic first, full check on release branch. Risk: customer friction for deprecations -> mitigation: clear migration guides and SDK helpers.

next_steps: 1) Harden compat-check CLI and add ABI binary checks. 2) Create Github Actions job to block merges and add maintainer override policy. 3) Implement Canary CD gate integration and dashboards. 4) Publish RFC and notify Dedicated/Private customers of new policy and pre-approval path. 5) Schedule tabletop runbook drill with SRE and on-call rotation.
owner_notes: This policy intentionally errs on the side of caution for hosted customers but provides clear opt-in paths for dedicated/private customers to accept faster changes. The compat-check tool is a living artifact and should allow whitelist overrides for platform teams while keeping public merges strict.
